FivemFramework.title: FiveM framework
FivemFramework.intro: The snailycad-framework FiveM resource sends ESX, QBCore and Qbox characters, their vehicles and duty changes to the CAD. Characters become citizens, owned vehicles become registered vehicles, and units go on or off duty with the player.
FivemFramework.lastSync: Last sync from a game server
FivemFramework.never: No game server has synced yet.
FivemFramework.enabledDescription: When off, the CAD ignores everything game servers send.
FivemFramework.syncCitizensDescription: Create and update citizens from game characters.
FivemFramework.syncDutyDescription: Set units on and off duty when players go on or off duty in game.
FivemFramework.setupInfo: Turn on the CAD API token (API Token tab). Install the snailycad-framework resource on your FiveM server, then run this in the server console with your token. See the docs: Integrations, FiveM framework.
FivemFramework.phonesIntro: In-game phones the snailycad-framework resource reads a character's phone number from. It reads every phone that's running; the CAD saves the number from the first one switched on here.
FivemFramework.phonesSyncOff: The FiveM framework sync is switched off, so no phone numbers are synced. Turn it on in the FiveM framework tab.
FivemFramework.phonesOrder: When several phones have a number, the first one switched on in this list wins. Switching a phone off only stops its number being used; nothing changes in game.
FivemFramework.phonesNotReported: Your game server hasn't reported its phones yet. Update the snailycad-framework resource and restart it (or run snailyframework_check) to see which are running.
FivemFramework.removedVehiclesDescription: When a synced vehicle is sold, deleted or otherwise leaves a garage in game (the resource notices within seconds).
FivemFramework.removedVehiclesUnlink: Keep them without an owner (their records stay)
